note: One composer per idea, one idea per beat. Pick by the transformation you want, not by habit; never repeat the same composer for two consecutive beats. Each is tuned for a 5–13 s window.

deconstruct.draws: A finished shot fills the frame, breaks into picture / sound / voice / captions, then closes back into one film and folds to a line.
deconstruct.use: The hook. Use it first when the point is that a finished video is made of parts you control.

editor.draws: The editor window builds itself, bin and inspector fill, clips drop onto the timeline, gaps close, the camera pushes into the viewer.
editor.use: Show the real editing surface: clips appearing, moving and being arranged.

assistant.draws: A request leaves the chat, an MCP beam reaches external harness chips that dock like extensions, the result flies back into the timeline.
assistant.use: The assistant as a client of outside harnesses. Only name integrations the build supports.

motionScene.draws: Code lines lift off and become geometry that assembles a shot; fills sweep in; the camera enters the finished scene.
motionScene.use: Code-to-video, deterministic scenes, or any 'this was generated' moment.

voiceWhisper.draws: Script card, local TTS waveform and mic rings, then Whisper returns a transcript card and synced caption words.
voiceWhisper.use: Local narration and automatic subtitles. Keep the local label honest.

assembly.draws: Four lanes converge, clips snap and gaps close, a timecode reaches the exact duration, the camera dives into the programme monitor for a montage, then pulls back.
assembly.use: The payoff: everything on one timeline, then the finished film playing.

close.draws: Mark and wordmark, one-line value, the honest licence/condition line, one call to action.
close.use: The last beat. Brand, what it is, what it costs, what to do next.

interlude.draws: Concentric rings, drifting particles and one short keyword with a rule.
interlude.use: A breath between two dense beats in a long film. Pass `word` in the beat to change the keyword; never use it twice in a row.
